# Airtable Omni Custom Interface Refiner

**A Claude skill that turns code generated by Airtable Omni into production-ready Interface Extensions.**

Omni gets you 80% of the way. This skill handles the 20% Omni can't: drag & drop, circular layouts, optimistic UI, field-ID discipline, permission checks, error states, dark mode, and the dozens of SDK gotchas you only learn after shipping extensions to clients.

Built from the playbook Airmakers uses across 50+ production Airtable extensions.

---

## What it does

When you paste Omni-generated code into Claude and ask it to add a feature, fix a bug, or harden it, Claude loads this skill and:

1. **Runs a health check** on your Omni output — reports what's broken, fragile, or non-resilient
2. **Applies a catalogue of canonical transformations** from static grid to circular layout, blocking writes to optimistic UI, hardcoded options to dynamic, etc.
3. **Avoids SDK hallucinations** — no more `useRecordById` (doesn't exist), no more `getFieldByName` (doesn't exist in Interface Extensions), no more REST API calls in a Blocks context
4. **Enforces production conventions** — field IDs not names, `getFieldIfExists()` with null handling, permission checks before writes, array-field spreading to prevent data loss, dark mode on every color class

## Install

### Option A — Claude Code (recommended)

Drop the whole folder into `~/.claude/skills/`:

```bash
cd ~/.claude/skills
git clone https://github.com/noamsay/airtable-omni-refiner.git
```

Claude Code auto-discovers skills in that folder. Start a new conversation and paste your Omni code — Claude will pick up the skill automatically when it sees Airtable-flavored code.

### Option B — claude.ai (Project instructions)

If you're on claude.ai (web) and can't use Claude Code skills, copy the contents of `SKILL.md` into your project's custom instructions, and paste the `reference/*.md` and `examples/` files into the project's knowledge.

### Option C — Inline with a single conversation

Paste the contents of `SKILL.md` at the top of your conversation, then attach your Omni code. Works for one-off refinements.

## Usage

Once installed, start a conversation with Claude and share:

1. Your Omni-generated code (paste it or attach the file)
2. What you want to change or add
3. (Ideally) your table IDs and field IDs

Claude will run the health check, present what's fragile, and then apply the transformations. See `examples/` for a complete before/after on a wedding seating plan (drag & drop, circular tables, VIP badges, optimistic UI).

## What's in here

```
airtable-omni-refiner/
├── SKILL.md                              # Workflow, non-negotiable rules, and the diagnosis pass. Always loaded.
├── reference/                            # Detail. Claude reads only what the task needs.
│   ├── sdk-patterns.md                   # Performance, custom properties, resiliency, state, user scoping, colors
│   ├── field-types.md                    # Read/write formats per FieldType; rendering with HTML + Tailwind
│   ├── coding-standards.md               # Structure, naming, imports, error handling, libraries, validation checklist
│   └── transformations.md                # The T1–T10 catalogue
├── examples/
│   ├── README.md                         # How to read the example
│   ├── wedding-seating-before.jsx        # Realistic Omni output
│   └── wedding-seating-after.jsx         # The same after the refiner pass
└── README.md                             # You are here
```

`SKILL.md` is the router: it stays small so it costs little to load on every trigger, and points at the one reference file a given task needs. The detail lives in `reference/`.
